issuer: Azad Jammu and Kashmir's licensing authorities (under the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1971)
note: Read 2026-10-31. Pakistan is kept by its regions; this is Azad Jammu and Kashmir's, which keeps its own law: the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1971, in the AJ&K Revised Volume as the AJK Law Department publishes it. No one may drive a motor car, otherwise than as a paid employee, until 18 (s. 4(1)(ii)); a private car licence is effective without renewal for up to three years (s. 11), a most and not a fixed term, so validYears is null. No fee was read: fee null. The Ordinance names the issuer only as the licensing authority, 'an authority empowered to grant licences under this Act' (s. 2(16)); no AJK licensing office's page was reached (ajk.gov.pk is behind Cloudflare, ajkpolice.gov.pk didn't answer).

sources.title: Azad Jammu & Kashmir Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1971 (AJ&K Revised Volume, Law Department, Azad Government of the State of Jammu and Kashmir)
sources.said: AZAD JAMMU & KASHMIR MOTOR VEHICLES ... a motor car, otherwise than as a paid employee, unless he has attained the age of eighteen years ... effective without renewal for a period upto three years in the case of a licence to drive a motor car or motor cycle otherwise than as a paid employee ... "licensing authority" means an authority empowered to grant licences under this Act
